summary: Black Rock Point light marks the Great Bras d'Or entrance on Cape Breton: a first tower of 1868, a 1978 Coast Guard tower, and a former keeper's house now a private residence.

access.note: Coast Guard property. Grounds open, tower closed. Drive partway down the access road, then walk from a gate (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Committee on Navigation Securities recommends a light for the Great Bras d'Or (register)
Board of Works awards $1,750 contract to Robert Purves to build the first light, 20 July 1867
First tower finished; one-storey building with three-sided window (Lighthouse Friends) or square tapered wooden tower with attached dwelling (register)
Keeper Donald Morrison died; his son Alexander (A.F. Morrison) looked after the light for a few years
Malcolm D. Morrison takes charge of the light
Second two-storey lighthouse, per the register; disputed (see resolved_conflicts)
Two-storey lighthouse with square lantern room built to replace the original (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Directory)
Current wooden tower built; third tower on the site
Old two-storey keepers' house sold in 1979 and moved to a private residence site
Octagonal metal lantern installed on the 1978 tower
Frank Kozera, the station's last keeper, left after the government refused to let him keep living in the dwelling under a lease agreement
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse, register entry 21835, 20 October 2017

corrections.why: The record's private owner belongs to the former two-storey keepers' house, moved in 1979. The present light is owned by the Coast Guard (Lighthouse Friends; Lighthouse Directory). Needs human review, since the record may describe the converted house.

The record's position says it comes from the Coast Guard List of Lights, but the longitude is about 45 m off the List's 060 23 29.8 W (-60.391611). The register's coordinates (46.30521 N, 60.39226 W) match the record instead. A human should decide which is right.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates a second two-storey lighthouse to 1925. Lighthouse Friends and the Lighthouse Directory date the two-storey tower to 1937 and say it replaced the first. The story gives both dates and leaves the choice open.

The register says the light was established in 1866 when a light was recommended, and that the first tower was finished in 1868. Lighthouse Friends gives a contract of 20 July 1867, and a tower finished in 1868. Both give 1868 for the first tower, so the record's 1868 stands.

The register calls the first building a square tapered wooden tower with an attached dwelling; Lighthouse Friends calls it a one-storey building with a three-sided window. Both are reported in the story.

The record's conflict ('sources differ on whether the light is still lit') is resolved by the Coast Guard list: the present light operates 24 hours a day, year round. The dark one is the old two-storey house tower, inactive since 1978 (Lighthouse Directory).

Register 10.8 m (building height), Lighthouse Directory 10.5 m (35 ft), Coast Guard list 12.4 m. The story gives the register and Directory figures and leaves the Coast Guard figure as a different measure.
The Coast Guard list gives 25.8 m and the Lighthouse Directory 23.5 m. The official list is used in facts; the Directory figure is mentioned in the story.

Lighthouse Friends says the old house was moved a couple hundred metres south. The Directory says about 1 km southwest. The register says moved around 1980 for eroding shoreline. All three are given in the story.

notes_for_editor: Sources: the register (via Heritage Guide), two Lighthouse Friends pages (the present light and the old house), the Coast Guard List of Lights, the Lighthouse Directory, and two Marine reports. The Canadian Coast Guard List gives 46 18 18.8 N, 060 23 29.8 W; the register gives 60.39226 W, which the record also uses. The 45 m longitude difference is noted in corrections; a human should choose. Keeper M. D. Morrison (1911 list) was checked on the page image (printed p. 235): the Black Rock Point row gives M. D. Morrison, appointed 8 June 1892, and the Black Rock row above it gives Chas. Robinson, a different station that is not used. A different station named 'Black Rock' (Digby or Annapolis area) appears in the same lists with Charles Robinson as keeper; it is not used. Lighthouse Friends' keeper list has Frank Kozera from 1977, but the register calls the present tower fully automated and built in 1978; this is flagged in the story and in the Kozera keeper note. Lighthouse Friends gives the Robert Purves contract as 1867 and the register gives 1866 for the recommendation; both are given. Lighthouse Friends prose calls the second keeper 'Alexander'; its list prints 'A.F. Morrison'; both are given. The CBC 2017 article did not load (timeout) and was not used. No wreck or rescue at Black Rock Point was found in the sources read: the register's general line about shipwrecks is used without naming any wreck, so the Storms chapter is omitted. The Marine reports for 1900 to 1924 name the station in keeper and light lists; no works or incidents at the light were found in them beyond the 1901 remark. Ownership: the record's private owner and access apply to the former keepers' house; the present light is Coast Guard property with the grounds open. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story now states three disagreements it had passed over. The Lighthouse Directory puts the light on the east side of the entrance; the Coast Guard list says south. Lighthouse Friends' history section says the lighthouse is reportedly owned by Island Lights Inc., while its visitor notes say the Coast Guard owns it; a human should check current ownership before any correction is made. Lighthouse Friends dates the engine building to 1977; the register and the Directory say 1978.
